pages.text: Landscapes are written by water. A river carries grains as fast as it flows, and drops them as it slows - the heaviest first. A small grain of radius r sinks at a steady speed v = (2/9)(ρ_s − ρ_f)g r²/μ: sand settles in minutes, clay in days.
That is why the ground is layered. A $(item)Sediment Core$() is a tube of those layers, oldest at the bottom: floods, droughts and ash falls in the order they happened.
